subject: FY 2024 Property Tax Classification
overview: The City Council established the FY 2024 property tax policy by maintaining a 1.75 commercial shift while rejecting residential and small commercial exemptions. The Council also approved a retroactive wage adjustment agreement for the firefighter union.

items.title: Committee Reports on Food Truck and Leaf Blower Ordinances
items.summary: Approved committee reports detailing revisions and planned legal reviews for both the food truck ordinance and the leaf blower ordinance.

items.title: International Human Rights Day Resolution
items.summary: Adopted a resolution celebrating International Human Rights Day on December 10, 2023, and endorsing a statement submitted by the Medford Human Rights Commission.

items.title: Fire Union Wage Adjustment
items.summary: Approved salary increases and waived future readings for a multi-year contract adjustment covering the firefighters union.

items.title: Dedication and Moment of Silence for Steve Maskell
items.summary: Dedicated the meeting to the memory of longtime Medford High School educator, coach, and administrator Steve Maskell following his passing.

items.title: Deed Restriction Amendment for 12 Dell Avenue
items.summary: Continued a petition to amend a deed restriction at 12 Dell Avenue to the December 12 meeting to allow petitioners and staff to explore alternative options.

items.title: Common Victualler License for Mei Ling's Restaurant
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license transfer for Mei Ling's Restaurant at 434A Salem Street under new ownership by Huali Enterprises.

items.title: FY 2024 Tax Classification Hearing
items.summary: Voted to adopt a 1.75 tax levy shift to commercial and industrial properties and voted against adopting both residential and small commercial exemptions.

items.title: Update on DPW Union Contracts
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting updates on DPW contracts after receiving word that retroactive pay meetings are scheduled.

items.title: Carr Park Construction Neighborhood Concerns
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the Community Development Office to meet with Carr Park neighbors to address park access and dog-walking concerns during winter construction.

items.title: Everett Soccer Stadium and Encore Casino Mitigation
items.summary: Approved a resolution calling on the city to study traffic impacts and pursue community benefits regarding a proposed Everett soccer stadium and adjacent Encore developments.

items.title: Loan Order for Carr Park Phase Two
items.summary: Approved the third reading of the loan order for Phase Two improvements at Carr Park.
